title: enhance-helm-templates-with-sequenced-init-pipelines-and-rollback-guardrails
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Introduce a tenant-scoped sequenced init pipeline and safe-rollback flags to the private installer Helm charts. Motivation: existing init hooks run concurrently per release which led to sporadic race conditions on tenant resources during multi-tenant upgrades and made rollbacks risky when migrations partially applied. This PR adds a lightweight sequencing layer in templates plus a small values schema extension to control pipeline stages, concurrency, and rollback behavior. Changes include: (1) new values keys under .Values.initPipeline to define ordered stages, per-stage timeouts, and 'waitFor: <k8sCondition>' expressions; (2) templating helpers (templates/_init-pipeline.yaml, templates/_pipeline-helpers.tpl) that render Job/JobTemplate groups with an annotation-based sequencer (release-annotations used as semi-transactional locks); (3) an optional preflight stage that runs a dry-run migration and checks CR readiness, gated by .Values.initPipeline.preflight.enabled; (4) a safeRollback boolean that, when true, switches post-upgrade hooks to non-destructive reconciliation-only jobs and preserves migration state in a release-scoped ConfigMap instead of tearing it down; (5) small values-schema additions to values.schema.json to validate new fields and document allowed stage names; (6) chart README additions and migration notes for operators. The design prioritizes backward compatibility: if .Values.initPipeline.enabled is unset or false we keep current hook behavior. Rollout plan: enable feature off by default, opt-in via values for Private installs, run canary installs in staging for two weeks, then flip default in a minor release after validation. Testing: unit template tests for the new helpers, integration smoke in CI (k3s) that simulates concurrent tenant upgrades, and a manual dry-run with on-prem QA. See commits and CI details below.

review_comments: Marco Li: Can you explain why we chose an annotation-based sequencer instead of leader-election via a controller? Concerned about robustness across kube api server restarts.

Priya Natarajan: Annotation locks are intentionally lightweight and avoid adding an operator process to the private installer. We added timeouts and a small jitter to minimize livelock. For larger installs we recommend using external orchestration; we also added guidance in README about switching to a controller if desired.
Elena Ortiz: Please validate values.schema.json changes with helm schema tests and add a clear migration note for operators who rely on pre-upgrade hooks.
Priya Natarajan: Added schema tests and expanded upgrade notes; included a sample values.yaml snippet for enabling safeRollback and a migration checklist.
Samir Patel: Will safeRollback leave behind ConfigMaps forever? We should include an explicit TTL policy or cleanup job.

Priya Natarajan: safeRollback preserves state for up to .Values.initPipeline.rollbackStateTtlDays (default 30). The cleanup job is included but disabled by default; operators can opt-in in values.yaml. Documented in README.
release_notes: Added optional sequenced tenant init pipeline with preflight dry-run, configurable per-stage timeouts, and safeRollback mode preserving migration state for safer rollbacks. Feature is opt-in; see chart README for migration steps and values examples.
notes_for_ops: Default behavior is unchanged; to opt-in set charts.private.initPipeline.enabled=true and configure stages in values.yaml.
safeRollback=true will change post-upgrade hooks to non-destructive reconcile jobs and store migration state in a ConfigMap for up to initPipeline.rollbackStateTtlDays days.
Operators should run the included k3s smoke test in staging and validate their migration scripts with preflight.enabled=true prior to enabling in production.
If you need stronger guarantees consider deploying the optional sequencer controller referenced in README (link in chart docs) instead of annotation-based locks.
